QuestionStmt.S: A rectangular block of surface area A emits energy E per second at 27°C. If length and breadth is reduced to half of initial value and temperature is raised to 327°C then energy emitted per second becomes

Solution.S:
Using Stefan-Boltzmann law: $P = \sigma \varepsilon A T^4$.

Initial: $E = \sigma \varepsilon A (300)^4$.

New area $A' = \frac{A}{4}$, new temperature $T' = 600$ K.

$$E' = \sigma \varepsilon \frac{A}{4} (600)^4 = \frac{A}{4} \times 16 \times (300)^4 \sigma \varepsilon = 4E$$

Thus the correct option is B: $4E$.
